title: Training-data default typeface
pattern: font-family\s*:\s*["']?(?:Inter|Roboto|Arial|Helvetica(?: Neue)?|Open Sans|Lato|Montserrat|Poppins|Plus Jakarta Sans|Space Grotesk|DM Sans|Outfit|Sora|Geist|Instrument Sans|Fraunces|Playfair Display)\b|fontFamily\s*:\s*["'`](?:Inter|Roboto|Arial|Poppins|Montserrat|Geist)\b|fonts\.googleapis\.com\/css2?\?family=(?:Inter|Roboto|Poppins|Montserrat|Open\+Sans|Lato|Space\+Grotesk|Plus\+Jakarta\+Sans|DM\+Sans|Outfit|Sora|Fraunces|Playfair\+Display|Instrument\+Serif|Instrument\+Sans)\b|import\s*\{[^}]*\b(?:Inter|Roboto|Poppins|Montserrat|Space_Grotesk|Plus_Jakarta_Sans|DM_Sans|Outfit|Sora|Fraunces|Playfair_Display|Instrument_Serif)\b[^}]*\}\s*from\s*["']next\/font\/google["']|@fontsource(?:-variable)?\/(?:inter|roboto|poppins|montserrat|space-grotesk|plus-jakarta-sans|dm-sans|outfit|sora|fraunces)\b|from\s*["']geist\/font
why: Inter, Roboto, Poppins, Space Grotesk, Fraunces and kin are what every generator reaches for, so the page reads as unchosen.
fix: Pick a face with a reason tied to the subject (or the project's DESIGN.md face); on dense app UI a tuned system stack is fine, but name it deliberately.

title: System/Inter sans as display voice
why: Headings set in the platform sans or Inter have no voice; the display role is where a page gets its character.
fix: Set h1/h2 in a display face via var(--font-display) and keep the workhorse sans for body and UI.

title: Gradient-clipped text
why: Gradient headline/metric text is decoration standing in for hierarchy and is one of the most recognised generated-UI tells.
fix: Use solid ink; get emphasis from size, weight or a display face.

title: Text under 11px
why: Functional text below 11px (and body below 12px) fails legibility on real screens; tiny decorative labels are a generated habit.
fix: Body 16px (min 14px in dense UI), labels/captions 12-13px; only legal smallprint may sit at 10-11px.

title: Letter-spacing 0.15em or more
why: Very wide tracking (tracking-[0.2em] micro-labels) breaks word shapes and is the signature of generated eyebrow labels.
fix: Body tracking 0; caps labels 0.06-0.1em max; drop the tracked caps label entirely where it is an eyebrow.

title: Tracking tighter than -0.04em
why: Past -0.04em letters collide and the display line loses legibility; it reads as trying too hard.
fix: Display 48px+: -0.02 to -0.03em; headings 32px+: -0.01 to -0.02em; never below -0.04em.

title: Eyebrow / kicker label above heading
why: A tiny tracked-caps label stacked over every heading is the default generated SaaS section opener; Impeccable, Hallmark and taste-skill all ban it.
fix: Delete it and let the heading carry the section; fold any real information into the heading or the first sentence.

title: One accented word in a heading
why: Setting one headline word in italic serif, colour or gradient is a 2025 generated-hero signature.
fix: Set the whole heading one way; get emphasis from a line break or a second line at a second size.

title: Full sentence at display size
why: A 9+ word headline blown up to text-6xl+ wraps to 3-4 lines and eats the first viewport.
fix: Keep display headlines to about five words (two lines max); move the rest into a lede at body-plus size.

title: Monospace as a 'technical' costume
pattern: (?<![\w-])font-mono(?![\w-])|font-family\s*:\s*["']?(?:JetBrains Mono|IBM Plex Mono|Space Mono|Geist Mono|Fira Code|DM Mono|Roboto Mono|SF Mono|ui-monospace|monospace)\b
why: Mono micro-labels, captions and meta rows are a gallery fashion copied by generators; mono should mean code, data or measurement.
fix: Set labels in the body face a step smaller in sentence case; keep mono for code and tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).

title: Purple/indigo or blue-cyan Tailwind gradient
why: The two-stop purple-to-blue / blue-to-cyan 'trust' gradient is the single most recognised AI-UI colour tell.
fix: Use one flat, deliberate brand colour (mixed in OKLCH for this product); if a gradient must exist, keep it single-hue and functional.

title: Violet/indigo or blue-cyan CSS gradient
why: Hard-coded violet/indigo gradients and the blue-to-cyan two-stop are the canonical generated hero and button fills.
fix: Replace with a flat surface in the project's accent token; reserve gradients for a functional scrim over a photo.

title: Tailwind default indigo/violet as accent
why: indigo-500/600 (#6366f1, #4f46e5) and violet-500/600 are the textbook model-default accent; nobody chose them.
fix: Take the accent from DESIGN.md (var(--accent)); if none exists, mix one in OKLCH from the product's subject, not the framework palette.

title: Pure #000 / #fff surfaces and ink
why: Untinted absolute black/white vibrates against each other and reads as framework default rather than a palette.
fix: Tint toward the brand hue: e.g. #0f0f0f / #fafafa (or OKLCH chroma >= 0.005); dark text ~#111, light text ~#f0f0f0.

title: Gray text on a saturated background
why: Neutral gray on a coloured fill looks washed out and usually fails 4.5:1.
fix: Use a darker shade of the background hue, or near-white, for text on colour; verify 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large.

title: Cream ground + terracotta accent
why: The 'warm editorial' fix for purple slop (cream paper, serif display, clay/terracotta accent) became the third-wave generated look.
fix: Move one axis: change the accent first, then the paper; derive warmth from the subject's real materials, not cream + clay.

title: Coloured glow shadow
why: Zero-offset chromatic halos (neon on dark) are the default 'cool' generated effect, not a depth system.
fix: Use neutral elevation (offset + blur, e.g. 0 1px 2px / 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.08-.16)) or express depth with a lighter surface step.

title: Radial halo / blurred colour orbs
why: Floating blurred blobs and chromatic radial spotlights behind the hero are reflex decoration, the gradient cousin of the glow.
fix: Let the surface stand: a solid or subtly stepped background, or a real image; light the composition with one deliberate material accent.

title: Three equal feature cards
why: Hero followed by three identical icon+heading+text cards is the stock generated section; it signals no content decision was made.
fix: Use the number of items the content actually has and vary the composition: lead item large, list or table for the rest, or an inline demo.

title: Everything centred
why: Centring every section (taste-skill warns above ~72%) removes the shared left edge that makes a page look composed.
fix: Left-align running content on 2-3 reused x-positions; keep one centred moment (hero or closing statement) at most.

title: 100vh / 100vw sizing
why: 100vh jumps under mobile browser chrome and 100vw adds horizontal scroll when a scrollbar exists.
fix: Use 100svh/100dvh (h-svh, min-h-dvh) for heights and width: 100% for full-bleed; add overflow-x: clip on html/body.

title: Stock landing-page section order
why: Hero → Features → Testimonials → Pricing → FAQ/CTA in that order is the generated landing skeleton.
fix: Order sections by the argument the product needs to make; add at least one non-stock section (inline demo, comparison against the status quo, full-bleed proof).

title: Decorative 01 / 02 / 03 numbering
why: Zero-padded index numbers on sections or steps are editorial scaffolding copied from award sites; they carry no information.
fix: Order by position, scale or the words; use a semantic <ol> when it truly is a sequence.

title: Rounded icon tile stacked above heading
why: A small rounded-square icon container above a card heading is the universal generated feature-card template.
fix: Put the icon inline beside the heading (no container), or drop the icon and let a real image or the type carry the card.

title: Coloured side-stripe border
why: A thick coloured border-left on cards, callouts and alerts is the most recognisable generated dashboard tile.
fix: Drop the stripe: signal state with a tinted background, an icon plus label, or a 1px full border.

title: Soft rounded shadow cards everywhere
why: Every card wearing rounded-2xl + shadow-xl (or a hairline border plus a wide shadow, the 'ghost card') is a default nobody chose.
fix: Declare elevation once: either a defined edge or a soft shadow; resting cards get a tone step, not a shadow; card radius 12-16px.

title: Glass / backdrop-blur everywhere
why: Translucent blurred panels on many elements are first-wave generated decoration, not a specific effect.
fix: One sticky bar may blur; make cards opaque surfaces one tone step from the ground.

title: Hand-drawn traffic-light window chrome
why: Three red/yellow/green dots over a styled-div 'screenshot' fake a product instead of showing it.
fix: Show a real screenshot or the real component in a plain <figure>, with no drawn OS chrome.

title: 'New / Introducing' pill above hero
why: A pill chip announcing 'New' or 'Introducing' over the headline is the default generated SaaS hero opener.
fix: Say the news in the supporting sentence, or link one real announcement from the nav.

title: Emoji standing in for icons
why: Emoji (and unicode glyphs) as feature icons or bullets are an instant generated tell and render inconsistently across platforms.
fix: Use one SVG icon library (or authored SVG) at a single 1.5-1.75px stroke with currentColor, or no icon at all.

title: Sparkle / rocket emoji in UI copy
why: ✨🚀⚡🎯 sprinkled through headings, buttons and bullets is the hype register of generated marketing pages.
fix: Remove them; say the specific thing in words, and use real icons only where an icon aids scanning.

title: Placeholder image / avatar services
why: Hotlinked placeholder photos and random-face avatars are fragile, obvious, and usually prop up invented testimonials.
fix: Ship real, verified assets (local files with credit) or a deliberate empty-image slot; never random faces for quotes.

title: Broken or empty image source
why: Empty or dummy src ships as a broken-image box.
fix: Point at a real asset or remove the element; reserve space with aspect-ratio instead of a fake src.

title: Stock marketing verbs and adjectives
pattern: \b(?:unlock(?:s|ing)?\s+(?:the|your|new)|unleash(?:es|ing)?|supercharg(?:e|es|ed|ing)|seamless(?:ly)?|elevat(?:e|es|ing)\s+(?:your|the)|empower(?:s|ing)?|revolutioni[sz](?:e|es|ing)|game[- ]chang(?:er|ing)|cutting[- ]edge|next[- ]gen(?:eration)?|world[- ]class|best[- ]in[- ]class|industry[- ]leading|enterprise[- ]grade|mission[- ]critical|future[- ]proof|all[- ]in[- ]one|effortless(?:ly)?|blazing(?:ly)?[- ]fast|lightning[- ]fast|reimagin(?:e|ed|ing)|streamlin(?:e|es|ed|ing)|harness the power|leverage the power|transform (?:the way|your)|to the next level|say goodbye to|delve|tapestry|synergy)\b
why: Unlock/seamless/elevate/supercharge/cutting-edge could describe any product, so they say nothing and mark the copy as generated.
fix: Replace with the specific verb and noun of what the product does ('Book a table', 'Sync invoices nightly').

title: Filler openers
pattern: \bin today['’]?s\s+(?:fast[- ]paced|digital|ever[- ]changing|modern|competitive|rapidly)|\bin (?:the|an) ever[- ](?:evolving|changing)\b|\bbuilt for the modern\b|\bthe future of \w+ is (?:here|now)\b|\blook no further\b|\bwhether you['’]?re an? \w+(?: \w+)? or\b|\bwelcome to the future\b|\bgone are the days\b
why: 'In today's fast-paced world' and 'Built for the modern team' are throat-clearing that precede no information.
fix: Delete the opener and start with the concrete claim or the action.

title: Rebuttal / 'not just X' cadence
why: Repeated 'Not a feature. A platform.' / 'X. No Y.' aphorisms are AI cadence; once is voice, the pattern is the tell.
fix: State the claim plainly once; vary sentence shapes; cut manufactured contrasts.

title: 'Get started' + 'Learn more' CTAs
pattern: >\s*(?:Get started(?: free| now| today)?|Learn more|Start (?:your )?free trial|Book a demo|Request a demo|Explore now|Discover more|Click here|Read more|Sign up(?: free| now)?|Try it free|Submit)(?:\s*(?:→|->|→|›|»))?\s*<
why: Label pairs that name no action ('Get started' / 'Learn more') are the generated hero default.
fix: Name the action or object: 'Start tracking', 'See the plans', 'Book a table'; one primary, at most one secondary.

title: Invented metrics, ratings and user counts
why: '10,000+ happy customers', '10x faster', '99.99% uptime' and five-star rows with no source are fabricated proof and a recognised tell.
fix: Use real, sourced numbers from the brief or a clearly labelled placeholder; otherwise show the product working instead of claiming.

title: Lorem ipsum and placeholder people
pattern: \b[Ll]orem [Ii]psum\b|\b[Dd]olor sit amet\b|\b[Ff]eature (?:[Oo]ne|[Tt]wo|[Tt]hree|[123])\b|\b[Pp]laceholder (?:text|copy|content)\b|\b[Ss]ample (?:content|text)\b|\b(?:[Yy]our|[Ii]nsert) (?:text|content|headline|title|copy|tagline) here\b|\b[Ii]mage (?:here|placeholder)\b|\b(?:John|Jane) (?:Doe|Smith)\b|\bAcme(?: Inc\.?| Corp\.?| Co\.?)?\b|\bFirstname Lastname\b|\b123 Main St(?:reet)?\b|\bSarah (?:Chen|Johnson)\b|\bAlex (?:Rivera|Chen)\b|\bEmily Rodriguez\b
why: Filler words and stock personas (Jane Doe, Acme, Sarah Chen) ship as obviously unfinished, generated work.
fix: Write real or plausible product-specific content at full density and list every sample detail for the client to confirm.

title: Em-dash habit
why: Em dashes at a density of several per screen are an AI cadence marker; one or two read as writing.
fix: Use full stops, commas, colons or parentheses; keep at most one or two em dashes per page.

title: Performative labels and furniture text
pattern: \b(?:[Ff]ield [Nn]otes|[Qq]uietly trusted by|[Oo]n our desks|[Ss]croll to (?:explore|discover)|[Aa]vailable for (?:work|projects|freelance)|[Ee]st\.\s?20\d\d|(?:[Ss]ecurity|[Pp]roductivity|[Cc]ompliance|[Pp]rivacy|[Ss]ales|[Dd]esign) theat(?:er|re))\b|\((?:[Ss]croll)\)|[^\s<>"'`]\s+·\s+[^\s<>"'`][^<·\n]{0,40}\s+·\s+[^\s<>]
why: 'Field notes', 'Quietly trusted by', 'Scroll to explore', 'Available for work', 'X theater' and A · B · C meta strings are decoration pretending to be content.
fix: Use plain section names ('Pricing'); delete scroll cues, status furniture and middot meta strings, or turn a real fact into a caption.

title: transition: all
why: Animating 'all' transitions layout and colour properties you never meant to, causing jank and accidental motion.
fix: List properties: transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), opacity 200ms (Tailwind: transition-[transform,opacity] or transition-colors).

title: Bounce, elastic or pulsing CTA motion
why: Bouncing chevrons, pulsing buttons and overshoot curves feel dated and demand attention the content has not earned.
fix: Use exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), ease-out-quart/expo) with no overshoot; no looping attention animation on CTAs.

title: ease-in or scale(0) entrances
why: ease-in starts slow so UI feels laggy; popping in from scale(0) looks cartoonish.
fix: Enter with a strong ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) from scale 0.95-0.98 + opacity 0; exits ~20-30% faster than entrances.

title: Same fade-up on every block
why: An identical fade-and-rise on every section is generic choreography, not an authored moment.
fix: Author one focal sequence for the page; keep other content visible by default, reveal at most once and under 900ms.

title: Decorative pulsing status dot
why: Pulsing 'live' / 'Available for work' dots simulate liveness decoratively.
fix: Use a static dot with a clear text label; pulse only when bound to genuinely live, changing data.

title: Marquee, typewriter or blinking caret
why: Auto-scrolling logo strips and fake typing heroes demand attention, hide content, and hold the headline unreadable.
fix: Show content static and whole; if a strip must move, pause on hover/focus and provide a control for anything past 5s.

title: Content hidden until JS reveals it
why: Reveal classes that start at opacity 0 ship a blank page when the script or observer fails.
fix: Visible by default: scope hiding under a .js class or animate from visible with @starting-style.

title: Motion with no reduced-motion path
why: Translate/scale/parallax motion without a prefers-reduced-motion path can trigger vestibular symptoms.
fix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) (or motion-safe:/motion-reduce:, useReducedMotion) that removes movement but keeps opacity/colour state changes.

title: Focus outline removed with no replacement
why: Removing the outline without a :focus-visible ring fails WCAG 2.4.7 and strands keyboard users.
fix: Keep a visible :focus-visible ring >= 2px at >= 3:1 contrast, shown instantly (e.g. focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2).

title: Click handler on a non-interactive element
why: A <div onClick> is not focusable, has no role and ignores Enter/Space.
fix: Use <button type="button"> (or <a href> for navigation); only if impossible add role, tabIndex=0 and key handlers.

title: Image without alt
why: Images without alt are announced as filenames or skipped with no context.
fix: Add alt describing what the image shows in context; use alt="" for purely decorative images.

title: <a> without href
why: An <a> with no href is not a link: not focusable, not keyboard operable.
fix: Give it a real href, or make it a <button> if it performs an action.

title: Pinch-zoom disabled
why: Blocking zoom fails WCAG 1.4.4 for low-vision users.
fix: Use <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"> with no maximum-scale or user-scalable.

title: Autoplay video without muted
why: Unmuted autoplay is blocked by browsers (the hero stays frozen) and startles users.
fix: Use autoplay muted loop playsinline plus a poster; give anything moving past 5s a visible pause control.
